source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 111: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions and safety: treat this as a diagnosis, not proof of a root cause. The backend, launcher, library and driver versions, world size, host placement, scheduler, container privileges, fabric, selected interface, topology, and blocked initialization stage are unknown; record them and label each value measured or estimated. Work only in an authorized isolated allocation, redact endpoints and credentials, use a finite watchdog, and clean up processes and temporary state. Variant 111 is not evidence of any platform-specific failure.

Baseline and measurements: assign a run ID and capture per-rank host, global/local rank, expected and observed membership, PID, device mapping, software/configuration hashes, rendezvous/store identifier (redacted), process-group and collective entry/exit timestamps, last-progress time, stderr, backend debug logs, GPU/NIC identifiers, interface/address/route/DNS/MTU/firewall state, peer-access status, PCIe/NVLink topology, container device and shared-memory visibility, ulimits, and clock-synchronization status. Confirm every expected rank starts exactly once, uses the same rendezvous endpoint and world size, and enters collectives in the same order. Do not infer success from process existence alone.

Falsifiable hypothesis: a rank-specific rendezvous or transport mismatch (wrong membership, duplicate/missing rank, inconsistent interface/address, or blocked route) prevents all ranks from completing the first collective. This predicts that logs and timestamps will identify a missing or stalled rank and that a minimal same-dtype all-reduce will fail or exceed a short timeout under the suspect configuration. It is falsified if all ranks have matching membership, rendezvous, interface and collective order and the minimal test completes repeatedly while the full job still hangs; then investigate collective-order divergence, topology/peer access, resource exhaustion, software incompatibility, or workload-specific behavior.

Controlled experiment: with identical software, data, resource limits, and randomized run order, compare (1) one node, (2) a reduced world, and (3) the full world; in each, run a bounded process-group init followed by a small all-reduce and a barrier, with explicit timeout and per-rank logs. Repeat enough times to separate intermittent faults, and make one controlled change at a time (interface selection, topology placement, or world size). Record init/all-reduce latency, timeout/hang, rank failure, correctness/checksum, transport error, and cleanup outcomes with denominators. A passing reduced test localizes but does not exonerate the full fabric.

Decision and rollback: stop on timeout, unexpected rank, checksum mismatch, device reset, or unsafe resource growth; preserve diagnostics, terminate only the authorized test allocation, and revert any temporary environment or interface override. Do not change production topology, firewall, driver, or collective settings without owner approval. Report competing explanations and the evidence that would distinguish them. Claim a root cause only when the predicted signal reproduces and disappears under a controlled reversal; otherwise mark the result unresolved and require more evidence.

quality_dimensions.coverage: covers assumptions, rank/rendezvous/interface/topology checks, hypothesis, controlled comparison, confounders, measurements, failure denominators, safety, and rollback
quality_dimensions.technical_correctness: provisional; avoids platform-specific claims and separates localization from causal proof
quality_dimensions.falsifiability: explicit prediction and reversal-based falsification criterion
quality_dimensions.measurement_plan: per-rank logs, timestamps, environment, latency, correctness, timeout, transport, and cleanup outcomes
quality_dimensions.boundary_conditions: single-node, reduced-world, full-world, intermittent faults, duplicate/missing ranks, and workload-specific divergence
quality_dimensions.safety: authorized isolated allocation, redaction, bounded watchdog, cleanup, and approval gates

risks: NCCL/backend-specific diagnostics and timeout semantics vary by version and launcher
a passing reduced-world test can miss full-fabric or topology faults
timestamps and logs may be incomplete or clock-skewed
environment changes can mask rather than repair an intermittent fault
evidence_required: per-rank membership and rendezvous records
backend transport/debug logs with redacted endpoints
GPU/NIC/interface/topology and container visibility snapshots
repeated randomized matched minimal-collective results for all three world sizes
checksums and separate timeout/rank-failure/cleanup denominators
controlled reversal showing whether the hypothesized change restores behavior
